title: Mashmanock
summary: Mashmanock is a Southampton placename connected with Canoe Place Creek near the Canoe Place isthmus and Shinnecock Canal. The name is also cross-referenced to Mashomuck, and a later Toyonge entry creates a location question by associating the 1648 deed reference with Red Creek.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Canoe Place/Shinnecock Canal point; exact Mashmanock location remains uncertain because of Toyonge/Red Creek cross-reference.
translation_content:
The name is interpreted as a place where a boat or canoe is moved or dragged, matching the Canoe Place association. The text gives Mash-mom-ock as the linguistic form and points readers to Mashomuck for comparison.

Why Place Names Matter

“Many geographic names reflect a feature’s early or longstanding association with a commercial enterprise or a prominent business person.”

— U.S. Board on Geographic Names, Principles, Policies, and Procedures: Domestic Geographic Names (2022), PDF page 38
whereintheworld_content: This blue marker is an approximate general-location point for Canoe Place near the Shinnecock Canal. It is not an exact historic creek coordinate, and the Red Creek/Toyonge cross-reference should be reviewed before using a more specific marker.
